papers.title: The Alma catalog of OB stars. IV. A massive star census of the Magellanic Clouds System
papers.abstract: Context. The Magellanic Clouds System (MCS), comprising the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC) and the Magellanic Bridge (MB), offers a nearby laboratory for studying massive stars. Existing catalogs are limited by extinction, crowding, and incomplete cross-validation with the literature. Aims. We identify candidate stars with initial masses of roughly 8 solar masses or more, including O- and early-B-type stars, supergiants, luminous blue variables, and Wolf-Rayet stars. We aim to improve completeness in reddened and crowded regions and recover sources missed by large surveys. Methods. We combine Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry with SIMBAD, HST, and complementary optical and infrared surveys. We select candidates using color-magnitude and color-color diagrams, extinction tracks, Gaia astrometry and variability, and spectral classifications. We check for duplicates and multiple systems, include literature and HST-resolved sources without reliable Gaia counterparts, especially in 30 Dor, and derive synthetic Gaia photometry where Gaia measurements are incomplete. Results. ALS IV contains 51 954 massive star candidates: 36 506 in the LMC, 15 264 in the SMC, and 184 in the MB. It provides homogeneous identifiers and coordinates, multiwavelength photometry, astrometry, variability diagnostics, and spectral classifications where available. Complementary photometry and HST observations recover reddened and crowded sources missed by Gaia-based selections. The sample traces the main massive-star populations and prominent star-forming regions across the MCS. Conclusions. ALS IV provides the most comprehensive census of massive star candidates in the MCS and serves as a reference for massive-star studies and future surveys and Gaia releases.

papers.title: A Wideband Technosignature Search of 210,191 Nearby Main-sequence Stars with the VLA Sky Survey
papers.abstract: Searches for radio technosignatures have concentrated on narrowband signals. We present a complementary search for excess broadband 2-4 GHz emission from 210,191 Gaia DR3 main-sequence stars within 100 pc in all epochs of the VLA Sky Survey (VLASS; 2017-2026). Cross-matching with the Epoch-1 catalog yields 51 high-reliability positional associations (versus 1.5 expected by chance). All but one are known natural emitters that, where measurable, move with their stars; the remaining source, near LSPM J1943+5337, is not at the star. Because stellar flares can mimic transmitters in continuum flux, a detection counts as a possible transmitter at any luminosity only at the 32,985 apparently single AFGK stars outside known radio-emitter classes, and at M dwarfs and AFGK multiples only above $10^{10}$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Forced photometry of 208,232 stars in all epochs finds 1 steady-test detection and 3 stars detected in at least one epoch among the eligible stars, against 1.3 and 1.9 expected by chance. The median per-star limit on steady emission is $L_ν<4.0\times10^{8}$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Without background subtraction, fewer than $1.5\times10^{-4}$ of eligible AFGK stars host a steady transmitter above $10^9$ W Hz$^{-1}$, and fewer than $2.3\times10^{-5}$ of all stars outside the known-emitter classes host one above $\sim1.1\times10^{10}$ W Hz$^{-1}$; counting every M-dwarf detection as a possible transmitter, fewer than $5.5\times10^{-4}$ of M dwarfs host one above $10^9$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Stacks detect population-averaged emission from M dwarfs, concentrated in those with activity evidence. Continuum surveys thus constrain broadband, modulated, or rapidly drifting signals that narrowband pipelines do not search for.

papers.title: Scalar-tensor interactions selected through their first-order thermodynamic dynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate the restrictive capability of first-order thermodynamics on scalar-tensor gravity. Starting from a general action containing nonlinear curvature dependence, an Einstein-tensor-Hessian coupling, and independent quadratic and cubic scalar-Hessian interactions, we derive the complete effective-fluid quantities. Simultaneously imposing Eckart's heat-conduction and shear-viscosity equations, while accounting for cancellations between interactions, substantially reduces the original operator basis and determines the geometric shear viscosity. Retaining the complete heat-conduction law, we establish an integrability condition that constrains the nonlinear Hessian interactions without prescribing the temperature and thermal conductivity. We construct explicit constitutive pairs and derive the associated thermal evolution, revealing contributions beyond the usual acceleration-aligned description. Remarkably, the thermodynamic integrability condition simplifies the scalar-metric kinetic structure such that imposing covariant degeneracy excludes the remaining nonlinear interactions, recovering the established luminal Horndeski subclass. Nonlinear thermodynamically compatible interactions nevertheless survive when degeneracy is restricted to the scalar-unitary gauge. These results establish a connection between thermodynamic integrability and dynamical degeneracy, demonstrating the potential of first-order thermodynamics as an independent and complementary criterion for selecting gravitational interactions.

papers.title: HEP-Ex-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Performance in High Energy Physics Experiment Data Analyses with Sealed Worlds
papers.abstract: Agentic systems are increasingly being explored for automating experimental high-energy physics measurements, but the correctness of their results can today be reliably evaluated only via extensive expert review. To address this, we propose a method to perform detailed quantitative evaluations of agent-driven analyses through the use of blind analysis and injection tests, which are critical in a typical expert review. Agents develop a data analysis pipeline on a public dataset, while the evaluation is performed on programmatically generated sealed private datasets where signals are injected and simulation settings varied within realistic detector uncertainties. By requiring agents to provide a single workflow that is evaluated across these "sealed worlds", we are able to test the accuracy and robustness of the workflows. We demonstrate the approach on four tasks built from CMS open data and present it as a way to reliably benchmark scientific work in experimental high-energy physics. At the time of writing, the best-performing model, Gemini 4 Argon, reaches 60% of the score of the expert reference analyses on average, ahead of GPT 6 Astra at 38% and Claude Opus 5.5 at 31%. In individual sessions on one of the tasks, Gemini 4 Argon exceeds the reference. The benchmark is hosted at https://hep-ex-bench.github.io

papers.title: VENUS: A Census of Strong Lensing in a 60-Cluster JWST Survey
papers.abstract: We present strong-lensing models for the 57 galaxy clusters observed in Cycle 4 out of the 60 targeted by the JWST Vast Exploration for Nascent, Unexplored Sources (VENUS) program. Models for the remaining three clusters will be incorporated after their observations. The dataset comprises 5013 individual images, corresponding to 1733 multiply-imaged systems, of which 912 have spectroscopic redshift measurements and 227 are newly identified. Using this new wealth of observations, we construct parametric lens models with our $\mathtt{AstroLensPy}$ software, reproducing the observed image positions with an average image-plane precision $Δ_{\rm RMS}$ of $0.54''$. With a total imaging area of $576$ arcmin$^2$, VENUS offers the largest homogeneous set of cluster strong-lensing models to date. The clusters yield a combined area of $191$ arcmin$^{2}$ magnified by $|μ|\geq3$ for a source $z_s=10$, for example, establishing the VENUS fields as a premier survey for high-redshift studies. Among our sample, the clusters MACS J0717.5+3745, RXC J0600.1-2007 and PLCK G287.0+32.9 display the largest Einstein radii ($\geq 60''$) and magnified areas ($\mathcal{A}_{z_s=10}^{|μ|\geq3} \geq 9$ arcmin$^2$) for a source $z_s=10$, and therefore constitute the most potent gravitational telescopes known to date. Finally, leveraging the statistical power of the sample, we derive scaling relations between various lensing observables (Einstein radius, magnified area, projected mass) and the SZ/X-ray-inferred cluster mass, $M_{500,c}$.

papers.title: A catalog of Gaia DR3 luminous blue variables and candidate luminous blue variables
papers.abstract: Galactic LBVs are rare, evolved massive stars whose defining evidence is long-term spectroscopic and photometric instability, including S Doradus-type cycles, and, in exceptional cases, giant eruptions. Candidate LBVs (cLBVs) share LBV-like spectra and/or circumstellar nebulae; however, they lack long-term observational datasets that would detect their long-term variability and confirm their classification as bona fide LBVs. Modern time-domain surveys provide homogeneous light curves for many Galactic massive stars, but each survey has its own limitations in terms of depth, temporal coverage, and observing cadence. Using confirmed Galactic LBVs as a control sample, we aim to test what Gaia DR3 and complementary photometric surveys can and cannot establish about LBV-type variability. We assembled a vetted sample of 75 Galactic LBVs and cLBVs with near- and mid-infrared photometry from 2MASS, MSX, WISE, GLIMPSE, and MIPSGAL. The infrared material was used to validate identifications, evaluate source confusion, and place objects in a circumstellar-dust context. We then constructed light curves from Gaia DR3, the Bochum survey, the ASAS SN, and the ZTF, and analyzed large-amplitude and periodic cases with Lomb-Scargle (LS) and phase dispersion minimization (PDM) methods. Gaia DR3 matches are available for 67% of the sample and 76% are reported as variable. We identify high-amplitude variables and periodic systems that may be binaries rather than classical LBVs. Six confirmed LBVs and five candidates show variations larger than 0.6 mag in the Gaia RP filter. Their light curves are examined and three periodic variables are identified. The light curves of OMN2000 LS1 and DWC2011 140 show primary and secondary minima, strongly suggesting eclipsing binary systems. OMN2000 LS1 has a well-constrained period of 80.29 d, and DWC2011 140 of 95.07 d.

papers.title: Machine learning for trigger, reconstruction and generation
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly embedded in every stage of the LHC data-processing chain, from event generation to final reconstruction. This contribution reviews the latest ML developments from the ALICE, ATLAS, CMS and LHCb collaborations that were made public in the year preceding LHCP2026, following the workflow of the experiments: event generation and detector simulation, real-time trigger selection, and online/offline reconstruction. Highlights include generative models that accelerate the simulation of specific ALICE detector components by up to six orders of magnitude, the CMS AXOL1TL and ATLAS GELATO unsupervised anomaly- detection triggers now operating in Run 3, a quantised Deep Sets jet tagger for the CMS Phase-2 Level-1 trigger, ML-based jet energy correction and flavour tagging at LHCb, the first empirical scaling laws for transformer-based flavour taggers in ATLAS, and several transformer and graph- based reconstruction algorithms (ATLAS GN3 flavour tagging and MaskFormer tracking, LHCb GarNet, CMS MLPF) developed for HL-LHC operation.

papers.title: Phase-Resolved X-ray Polarimetry of LMC X-1: Enhanced Polarization at Inferior Conjunction
papers.abstract: We present a phase-resolved X-ray polarimetric analysis of the extragalactic black hole X-ray binary LMC X-1, a classical high/soft state source with a well-characterized accretion disk and an ionization cone/inferred jet. Previous X-ray polarimetry gave only orbit-averaged upper limits on the polarization fraction, leaving any orbital-phase dependence unexplored. We aim to probe how this polarization depends on orbital phase and to identify the origin of the polarized emission. We analyzed simultaneous IXPE, NICER, and NuSTAR observations taken in October 2022. We measured the polarization degree and angle in different energy bands as a function of orbital phase, performed spectro-polarimetric modeling to identify the emitting components, and modeled the phase modulation of the Stokes parameters with a cosine function. The polarization depends on orbital phase: during inferior conjunction (phase from -0.1 to 0.1), the polarization degree is (4.2+/-1.1)% in 2-3 keV and (3.4+/-0.8)% in 2-8 keV, with polarization angles of (46+/-8) and (50+/-7) degrees. Outside this phase it stays below the 99% minimum detectable polarization. The measured angle agrees with the ionization cone/jet direction (~45 degrees), and spectro-polarimetric modeling favors a soft-band origin for the polarization. The Stokes Q/I and U/I modulation is well described by a cosine at the orbital period and favors two spatially separated polarized components over a single one varying in amplitude. We also tested whether differential Faraday rotation of the disk light in an ordered magnetic field can reproduce the modulation and used it to place upper limits on the magnetic field. These results show that soft-band polarization of LMC X-1 appears only near inferior conjunction at a position angle aligned with the disk normal, and highlight the importance of orbital-phase sampling in polarimetric studies.

papers.title: Nuclear deep-inelastic scattering as a BSM probe via SMEFT
papers.abstract: Searches for New Physics at the energy frontier have motivated theoretical development of model-independent methods to constrain interactions beyond the Standard Model (BSM) like the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), as well as associated phenomenological analyses. While these approaches are powerful, they are also afflicted by the large space of higher-dimensional operators and the challenge of possible degeneracies among these operators. To help ameliorate these difficulties, processes beyond those at hadron colliders, including deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), have been identified and studied for their ability to contribute added constraining power. In this work, we extend such investigations to charged-lepton DIS involving heavy nuclei, for which we explore the systematics of SMEFT effects for a series of representative cases. In particular, we point out that nuclear effects can reshuffle the luminosities governing partons entering SMEFT-corrected hard interactions, such that the nucleus can serve as an expanded laboratory to explore SMEFT effects complementary to free-nucleon DIS. In particular, we find that nuclear DIS possesses significant constraining power over flavor-isovector SMEFT operator combinations, with reduced nPDF dependence; similarly, improved control over nPDFs would further enhance the SMEFT reach of nuclear DIS observables. We explore projections for future (proposed) facilities like the EIC, LHeC, and FCC-eh, finding that improvements to nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) can further sharpen the reach of nuclear DIS.

papers.title: Triple-Higgs production: a window on the Higgs potential and anomalous top-Higgs couplings
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of triple-Higgs production within the $κ$-framework as a probe of the Higgs potential and anomalous top-Higgs couplings. At leading order, we derive compact parametrisations of the inclusive $gg\to3h$ cross section in terms of the trilinear and quartic Higgs self-coupling modifiers $κ_3$ and $κ_4$, the top-quark Yukawa coupling modifier $κ_t$, and the anomalous two-top-two-Higgs and two-top-three-Higgs coupling modifiers $κ_{2t}$ and $κ_{3t}$. These parametrisations allow for a fast and accurate interpretation of current and future LHC measurements. Applying them to LHC Run 2 data and high-luminosity LHC projections, we quantify the impact of $κ_t$, $κ_{2t}$, and $κ_{3t}$ on the constraints on $κ_3$ and $κ_4$, and derive the first direct constraint on $κ_{3t}$ from existing LHC data. We further show that parameter points yielding nearly identical inclusive rates can give rise to different kinematic distributions, demonstrating the potential of differential measurements to resolve degeneracies and enhance the sensitivity of future triple-Higgs searches.

papers.title: Strong hyperbolicity of puncture-gauge formulations of gravitational theories with second order equations of motion
papers.abstract: We prove that the modified CCZ4 (mCCZ4) formulation, used in nonlinear puncture-gauge simulations of (d+1)-dimensional Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity and four-derivative scalar-tensor theory in four dimensions, is strongly hyperbolic for both theories at sufficiently weak coupling, provided that the gauge parameters are chosen to satisfy a cone-separation condition. The proof applies to the full principal symbol of the theories, extending previous analyses based on first-order perturbation theory about the Einstein limit. We establish strong hyperbolicity by recasting the mCCZ4 equations into a formally equivalent second-order system whose derivative structure resembles that of the modified harmonic formulation of Kovács and Reall. This allows us to adapt their covariant characteristic analysis and continuity argument, without assuming that individual eigenvalues or eigenvectors depend analytically on the coupling. We also show that standard CCZ4 in general relativity is strongly hyperbolic in puncture gauge away from two defective degeneracies.

papers.title: Scalar perturbations in extremal Reissner-Nordström geometry: new methods at work
papers.abstract: We study scalar radiation emitted by a particle moving along a circular orbit around a four-dimensional extremal Reissner-Nordström black hole. In particular, we calculate the energy fluxes carried by scalar waves to infinity and across the event horizon, as well as the scalar self-force acting on the particle, and express all these quantities as post-Newtonian expansions. Our results for the energy fluxes are in agreement with previous numerical findings in the literature. To solve the radial wave equation, we employ and test two distinct analytic approaches: the first is the so-called \textit{kink method}, a novel alternative stemming from quantum integrability and the second is the Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi method. The perfect agreement of the results highlights the potential of the kink method as a complementary tool for studying wave propagation in black-hole spacetimes.

papers.title: Holographic ensembles and giant gravitons at the Leigh--Strassler fixed point
papers.abstract: Finite-rank observables in holographic quantum field theories provide stringent tests of string and M-theory, but remain challenging to compute when supersymmetry is non-maximal. In this paper, we study the finite rank partition function of the $\mathcal N=1$ Leigh-Strassler CFT, which admits an interacting Fermi-gas description. We compute the partition function explicitly in two ensembles: the canonical ensemble at fixed rank $N$, and the grand canonical ensemble, where $N$ is summed over while its conjugate chemical potential $μ$ is held fixed. In line with recent proposals, we find that the perturbative large-$N$ and large-$μ$ expansions in both ensembles are reproduced by the on-shell action and one-loop determinant over Kaluza--Klein modes of type IIB supergravity, with appropriate ensemble-dependent boundary terms. Furthermore, the one-loop partition function of a D3-brane giant graviton precisely matches the leading nonperturbative correction to the boundary partition functions.

papers.title: CORALIE Radial Velocity Search for Companions around Evolved Stars (CASCADES) VI. Revised masses and homogeneous estimation of the stellar parameters of 583 red giants
papers.abstract: Giant-star radial-velocity surveys allow us to study how the exoplanet population varies with stellar mass and evolution. However, obtaining accurate estimates of stellar masses for such stars is challenging, as methods like isochrone fitting are prone to large errors due to the degeneracy associated with the closeness of isochrones. We provide a homogeneous re-derivation of the stellar parameters of the CASCADES giant-star survey. This includes parameters obtained from spectral energy distribution fitting, as well as an update of the stellar masses using asteroseismology. We use TESS light curves to measure the frequency of maximum oscillation power, $ν_{\rm max}$, for all the stars when applicable. We re-extract the stellar radii of the survey by fitting broadband photometry with ARIADNE, a spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting package, using priors from spectroscopy for the effective temperature, metallicity and $\log g$. By using scaling relations, we compute revised estimates of the stellar masses of targets with a $ν_{\rm max}$ measurement. We obtain new estimates of mass for 583 out of the 640 stars of the survey. These revised masses are typically 15 to 20% lower (median difference of $-0.35\,M_\odot$) than the ones obtained by isochrone fitting, in particular for low-metallicity stars for which this effect is stronger. These new masses impact the overall mass distribution of the sample, whose median decreases from $2.11\,M_\odot$ to $1.65\,M_\odot$. These revised masses provide the basis for future occurrence-rate analyses aiming to study the link between host-star mass and planet occurrence. They also highlight the uncertainties associated with the determination of masses for evolved stars.

papers.title: Hesperos & Eosphoros: A Coupled Differentiable Forced-Photometry Operator and Forward Model for SPHEREx Spectrophotometry
papers.abstract: We present Hesperos & Eosphoros, a forced-photometry operator and a forward model that, respectively, perform and model the spectrophotometric measurement of the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx). Implemented as GPU-accelerated, differentiable JAX programs, the two may be directly composed to measure the response of a downstream product (e.g., the galaxy density field) with respect to a modeled systematic or perturbation through the full measurement pipeline. We describe their design and demonstrate the composition on the response of an astrometric perturbation, and demonstrate how these may be used to generate direct measurement/pipeline response templates $\partial({\rm reconstructed\ density})/\partial({\rm systematic\ amplitude})$ for known image-level effects. Hesperos achieves a factor of $\sim700\times$ increased throughput per node-hour at production scale compared to the prior CPU-based Tractor measurement, previously the limiting step in the experiment's data processing, and propagates automatic derivatives through the full production measurement operator. We validate the measurement operator Hesperos against the public SPHEREx fork of The Tractor, and the forward model Eosphoros against the SPHEREx Sky Simulator and the renders themselves independently against GalSim. Taken together, this represents a powerful increase in capability for scaling, iterating, and optimizing galaxy clustering measurement pipelines.

papers.title: Constraining the Binary Fraction and Mass-Ratio Distribution of FGK Dwarfs with Gaia XP Spectra: Metallicity, $α$-Element, and Age Dependencies
papers.abstract: We present a study of the binary fraction and mass-ratio distribution for near 200,000 FGK dwarf stars within 1 kpc, utilizing the Stellar Locus Outlier (SLOT) method applied to synthetic Gaia XP photometry and stellar parameters from LAMOST DR9. By modeling the asymmetric color residuals relative to a metallicity-dependent single-star locus, we measure the binary fraction $f_b$ and constrain the power-law slope $γ_{\rm large\,q}$ of the mass-ratio distribution at high mass ratio $q$. Higher metallicity is associated with a steeper (more negative) $γ_{{\rm large}q}$, indicating a larger proportion of low-mass-ratio systems. For $α$-elements, [Mg/H] and [Si/H] are anticorrelated with $f_b$ in thin-disk-dominated subsamples; conversely, [Ca/H] shows a positive correlation with $f_b$ in thin-disk-dominated subsamples. No correlation is found between $f_b$ and $α$-element abundances in thick-disk-dominated subsamples. The binary fraction increases modestly toward older ages in the thin-disk population, a trend that likely reflects underlying correlations with chemistry. Our results shed light on how chemical composition and dynamical processes shape the binary properties of solar-type stars.

papers.title: Photometric Characterisation and Evolutionary State Investigation of the Low Mass-Ratio Contact Binary FASTT 1558
papers.abstract: Contact binaries with low mass ratios, as potential progenitors of stellar mergers, offer important insights into the physical processes governing mass and energy transfer. In this work, we present the first spectro-photometry based evolutionary investigation of FASTT 1558, a totally eclipsing, low mass-ratio contact binary. We combine TESS and ASAS-SN photometry with phase-resolved spectroscopy obtained with the 3.6m Devasthal Optical Telescope. The lightcurve modeling with PHOEBE shows that the system has an exceptionally low secondary-to-primary mass ratio of $q=0.1544\pm0.0013$, with a deep contact degree of $f=0.61\pm0.01$. Our analysis yields a total system mass of $1.92\pm0.31\,M_\odot$, while the distance to the system is estimated to be $648.45\pm29.85$ pc. Analysis of long-term eclipse timings reveals an apparent orbital period decrease of $\dot{P}=-(3.03\pm0.26) \times 10^{-7}$ ${\rm day\,yr^{-1}}$, which may be associated with mass-transfer from the primary to the secondary on a thermal timescale. The spectra show phase-dependent H$α$ and CaII equivalent widths, indicating a dynamically evolving chromosphere. Binary evolution calculations with MESA terminates through L2 overflow before reaching the observed low mass-ratio. Despite its extreme mass ratio, the system is presently Darwin stable, with $J_{\rm spin}/J_{\rm orb}=0.15\pm0.02$. FASTT 1558 therefore provides a robust observational benchmark for evolutionary models of low mass-ratio contact binaries.

papers.title: Holographic Mutual Information in an Anisotropic Field Theory
papers.abstract: We investigate holographic mutual information in an anisotropic strongly coupled plasma within the framework of gauge/gravity duality. Considering both parallel and perpendicular strip configurations, we analyze the effects of temperature, anisotropy, strip lengths, and separation distance on the correlation structure between subsystems. For strips with equal lengths, we show that increasing temperature suppresses mutual information and reduces the size of the correlated region in the phase diagram. We find that the parallel configuration exhibits a monotonic behavior. However, the perpendicular configuration displays a more complex behavior resulting from the competition between the effects of energy density and pressure. Similar qualitative features are observed for strips with unequal lengths. Our results suggest that the directional dependence of the energy density and pressure plays an important role in the behavior of mutual information and may explain the nontrivial directional effects observed in the phase structure.

papers.title: Longitudinal-dither wavefront sensing: Calibration-free measurement of mode mismatch
papers.abstract: Mode mismatch between a gravitational-wave detector and the beams injected into it lowers the power stored in the arms and the level of squeezing. Correcting it requires the complex amplitudes of the three second-order modes, measured on a calibrated scale with the cavity on resonance at its operating power. Here we present a method that obtains a signal proportional to the mismatch by moving the beam on the wavefront sensors already used for alignment control. A longitudinal dither of the cavity adds to the resonant mode a reference field, which reaches the sensors through the same signal chains and so calibrates both the scale of this signal and the Gouy phases of the sensors and actuators, with no external calibration. We demonstrate the method on an optical cavity held on resonance in its operating state at input powers of 2 W and 62 W. At 2 W it yields an optical model that agrees with independent measurements in the mode content, and with the layout model in the actuator Gouy phase within its uncertainty of about $1^\circ$. At 62 W the thermally induced change of the eigenmode is decomposed into waist-size and waist-position changes. The method requires only components that every controlled cavity already possesses and enables continuous in situ monitoring of the mode matching in the operating state.

papers.title: Casimir Experiments as Spin-Force Detectors
papers.abstract: Precision Casimir experiments enable highly sensitive probes of short range forces, but have thus far constrained only spin-independent interactions. We show that measurements between reversed polarizations of a magnetically compensated source enable direct searches of axion-mediated monopole-dipole forces. The spin force reverses sign, while the common Casimir, gravitational and electrostatic backgrounds broadly cancel. Compensated sources need no intervening shielding, allowing large probes at micrometer gaps. Casimir experiments could probe the couplings $g_p^e g_s^{N}$ and $g_p^e g_s^{e}$ at $λ\sim1-100~μ{\rm m}$ orders of magnitude beyond existing laboratory searches.

papers.title: The W Transform: an additional powerful tool for astrophysical time-series analysis
papers.abstract: This work introduces the W Transform (WT) for astrophysical applications and explores its similarities and differences to the Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT), in photometric stellar light curves (LCs). We tested both techniques on synthetic data, producing LCs with different noise levels and numbers of gaps, and applied them to LCs from TESS space mission. The analysis focused on six stars: the solar analog TIC 276293046, the ultra-cool dwarf TIC 359892714, the $γ$ Dor pulsator TIC 164173105, the eclipsing binary TIC 355151781, the hosting planet star TIC 142276270, and the brown dwarf TIC 102076870. Overall, the results were in agreement, except for stars with LCs presenting sector-to-sector differences in structures or changes in the number of gaps, reflecting time-dynamic effects in the same target, which affect how time-dependent variability features appear in the time-frequency representation. For such LCs, the WT spectra are more stable and accurate in recovering signal amplitudes than the CWT maps, which exhibit distortions and limitations, showing that the inherent flexibility of the WT method in adjusting the dominant frequency could enhance time resolution even in LCs with complex or variable structures. We conclude that the WT is a robust tool for the analysis of stellar LCs, and that both methods may complement each other in an in-depth analysis of a periodic astrophysical signal. The present results suggest that the WT is a robust and accurate tool for analyzing stellar LCs, expanding the range of numerical techniques available for analyzing different stellar periodic phenomena from photometric observations.

papers.title: When heavy vectors meet top partners: HVTP, a unified framework for composite Higgs searches
papers.abstract: Vector resonances and top partners are characteristic new states of composite Higgs models: they belong to the same strongly coupled sector, and partial compositeness ties their interactions to the mixings that generate the top mass. Experimental searches, however, usually treat them separately. We provide a common framework for both and release HVTP (Heavy Vectors and Top Partners), a public UFO model for MadGraph in which an electroweak triplet, a hypercharge vector and a colour octet couple to a custodial top-partner multiplet, with all couplings obtained from the exact diagonalisation of the mass matrices. The models and the inputs of our results are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24345218. We translate the latest LHC searches at 13 and 13.6 TeV into the parameter space of the model. In natural scenarios the top partners, which are directly tied to the Higgs mass and to the residual tuning, are lighter than the vector resonances; the vectors then decay mostly into partners and become broad: the standard searches lose much of their sensitivity, while the vectors produce partner pairs at rates that can exceed QCD production. For example, at our benchmark points, with partners near their present limits and an electroweak triplet at about 4 TeV, 73-83% of the triplet decays contain partners, and vector-mediated production reaches up to three times the QCD rate. At the HL-LHC this region can be probed by resonance searches extended to large widths and by partner-pair searches that include resonant production; the latter also reveal the partner spectrum. Composite Higgs models with a non-minimal coset generally also contain a pseudoscalar, which can alter the standard decays of the top partners; we include it in the extension HVTP_eta.

papers.title: Parallel and perpendicular: a two-population test with POSSUM radio galaxies confirms hint of CMB birefringence
papers.abstract: Analyses of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarisation find an isotropic rotation of the linear polarisation plane, cosmic birefringence, of $β\sim0.2^\circ$--$0.3^\circ$, hinting at parity-violating physics. An independent test at low redshift with different systematics is needed. Radio galaxies provide such a test because their Faraday de-rotated polarisation angle $χ_0$ is statistically aligned with their position angle $ψ$. Previous tests fitted only the population with $χ_0-ψ\approx90^\circ$. We add the population with $χ_0-ψ\approx0^\circ$, which is rotated by the same angle. We fit $χ_0-ψ$ with two axial von-Mises distributions plus a uniform background, with an unbinned likelihood including each source's angle error. We apply this to 33,298 components of 16,649 double radio sources from the Polarisation Sky Survey of the Universe's Magnetism (POSSUM), with both components at polarised S/N $>10$ and separated by more than half the beam. Both populations are equally abundant. In the CMB convention we measure $β=0.48^\circ\pm0.35^\circ$, agreeing with the CMB in sign and amplitude. Including the $0^\circ$ population halves the variance of $β$. Components closer than half a beam carry no information on the source axis; excluding them leaves $β$ unchanged and makes the two populations consistent in all morphological classes. Combining with the joint ACT and Planck likelihood for a late-time rotation yields $β=0.282^\circ\pm0.056^\circ$, $5.0σ$ from zero. At $z\sim0.5$, radio galaxies probe the rotation of the last $\sim$ 5 Gyr. A CMB-sized rotation there would point to a late-evolving field such as axion-like dark energy, whereas a rotation before reionisation, e.g. by axion-like dark matter, predicts $β\approx0$. Given absolute angle calibration, the full POSSUM survey can test the CMB result independently.

papers.title: Robustness of Transition Probabilities of Spectral Lines Deduced from Spatially Resolved Solar Spectra
papers.abstract: Atomic parameters are a key ingredient for the synthesis of spectral lines to model observed spectra and to extract meaningful physical information about the observed astrophysical object. We use quiet-sun observations to test the reliability of the atomic parameter inference from observed spectra. Our focus is on the transition probability of spectral lines, denoted as log(gf). We apply a spectropolarimetric inversion method to quiet-sun disc-centre observations at 1.56 $μ$m from the GRIS/GREGOR spectrograph. We use the coupled method implemented in the globin inversion code, where atomic parameters are spatially coupled, and a single value of these parameters is determined for every spectral line over the entire field of view. We carry out tests to determine the sensitivity of the inferred log(gf) values to various atmospheric parameters and the data reduction fallibility. We find that our log(gf) values are weaker by 0.023 dex compared to the most recent study. This is most probably caused by the constraint imposed on the log(gf) parameter due to the spatial coupling, lifting the degeneracy between temperature and log(gf). We use the Markov chain Monte Carlo method to determine the uncertainty in the inferred log(gf) values. For the strongest lines in the spectral region, the uncertainty in log(gf) is 1-4 %, increasing to 12 % for weaker and blended lines. Our tests suggest that the log(gf) values inferred using the coupled method from globin are robust against any local contamination to the observed line profiles, such as spectral stray light, and return a reliable and unique set of log(gf) values for the strongest lines irrespective of the chosen atmospheric model and observation dataset. This result is valid as long as the underlying assumptions of line formation under local thermodynamic equilibrium and the completeness of the line list are satisfied.

papers.title: From residuals to warps: Probing disk geometry with gas kinematics
papers.abstract: Evidence of shadowing among protoplanetary disks suggests that warped protoplanetary disks are widespread, making it crucial to constrain their three-dimensional shape in order to understand their dynamical evolution and origin. Yet, inferring this warp shape from observations is challenging, as the typical signatures of a warp, especially shadows, are often degenerate with the warp shape. Kinematics of disks may provide a method to recover the shape by interpreting the residuals from a Keplerian disk model as local changes in inclination and position angle. In this work, we test its applicability and limitations. We perform radiative transfer simulations of disks with a parametrized warp shape to create synthetic maps of $^{12}\mathrm{CO}$ rotational line emission at ALMA wavelengths and compare the fitted warp with the true warp shape. We find that the warp shape can be recovered for nearly face-on disks with small warp misalignments of a few degrees, even without knowledge about disk properties such as emission height. The overall warp shape remains traceable even at moderate spectral resolutions up to $0.8\,\mathrm{km/s}$. However, we identify regimes where the method breaks down, including disks with an inclination higher than $40^\circ$, a high emission height of the tracer, and sharp warp transitions. In addition, radial and vertical motions can introduce apparent warps and twists, motivating extensions of the method to account for these effects.

papers.title: Holographic Entanglement Entropy of Network CFT
papers.abstract: Miao et al. \cite{Guo:2025sbm, Guo:2026prm} proposed the AdS/NCFT correspondence, which explores the gravity dual of conformal field theories defined on networks. While previous studies investigated this model within Einstein and Gauss-Bonnet gravity (first- and second-order Lovelock gravity), in this paper, we generalize the framework to higher-order Lovelock gravity and more complex network structures. We derive the extremal and junction conditions for generalized Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) surfaces in third-order Lovelock gravity, which can be naturally extended to arbitrary higher-order Lovelock theories. Focusing on a network model comprising one node and three branches, we numerically investigate the relationship between the network holographic entanglement entropy (HEE) and gravitational coupling coefficients. Furthermore, by analyzing the HEE across various network configurations, we find that the primary structural feature affecting the network HEE is the presence of internal nodes within line-shaped networks. Our results indicate that the network HEE decreases as the number or depth of internal branches increases.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Quantum Error Mitigation for Bound-State Simulations
papers.abstract: Noise in quantum devices remains a major challenge for reliable quantum simulations, making quantum error mitigation an important tool for improving their accuracy. Machine learning-based quantum error mitigation (ML-QEM) provides a useful approach, but its performance depends on the training datasets and may produce reconstructed quantum states that are not physically valid. In this work, we introduce an ML-QEM framework that uses residual learning with convex projection to ensure that reconstructed density matrices satisfy physically valid density matrices. We study the effect of different training datasets and regression models using Haar-random and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) ansatz states. We compare the proposed approach with conventional ML-QEM, readout error mitigation, and zero-noise extrapolation. The method is tested on IBM quantum hardware for three- and four-qubit simulations of the bound $Λ$-deuteron and $Λ$-$α$ hypernuclear systems, respectively. For the three-qubit system, ridge regression trained on VQE-ansatz states gives a ground-state energy of -0.134 MeV, close to the ideal value of -0.135 MeV, with a state fidelity of 0.999. For four-qubit system, kernel ridge regression gives ground-state energies of -3.014 and -3.045 MeV, with corresponding state fidelities of 0.995 and 0.998. These results show that physically constrained reconstruction, along with the choice of training datasets and regression models, can improve ML-QEM performance for the quantum simulations studied in this work.

papers.title: Beyond the Thermodynamic-Volume Limit in Holographic Complexity
papers.abstract: In the large black hole regime, holographic complexity obeys a thermodynamic-volume scaling law, while the finite-size approach to this limit remains unresolved. In this Letter, we develop an analytic description of finite-size corrections to this scaling for complexity of formation in the complexity=volume (CV) proposal of odd-dimensional equal-spinning Myers-Perry-AdS black holes. We find that the leading finite-size correction retains state dependence that is absent from the limiting thermodynamic-volume law. This correction changes sign at a distinguished Critical Horizon Ratio (CHR), where the generic leading finite-size contribution vanishes and convergence to the thermodynamic-volume law is correspondingly accelerated. We further determine the dimension dependence of the CHR analytically, showing that it approaches a finite nonextremal value at large dimension with a calculable leading finite-dimensional correction. These results show that the finite-size approach can provide a new probe of holographic structure, motivating its exploration across different realizations of holographic complexity and its eventual characterization in the dual field theory.

papers.title: Topological Phase Transition of $ F_{α}{}^{γ} F^{αβ} F_{β}{}^{η} \ F^{λμ} R_{γηλμ} $ AdS Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic criticality and topological properties of four-dimensional charged anti-de Sitter black holes in the presence of a nonminimal electromagnetic-curvature interaction of the form \(F_α{}^γF^{αβ}F_β{}^ηF^{λμ}R_{γηλμ}\). Treating the coupling perturbatively to first order, we construct the corrected black hole solutions and derive their thermodynamic quantities in the extended phase space. Conventional critical behavior is examined through the criticality conditions for the Hawking temperature in both canonical and grand canonical ensembles. We then use thermodynamic topology to investigate the global structure of equilibrium configurations and its dependence on the thermodynamic parameters. In the canonical ensemble, two distinct regimes emerge: a noncritical region characterized by a total winding number \(W=+1\), and a critical region with \(W=0\). In the grand canonical ensemble, three distinct regimes are identified according to the electric potential. Interestingly, the low- and intermediate-potential regions share the same topological number, \(W=+1\), although conventional critical points occur only in the intermediate-potential region. The high-potential region, by contrast, is characterized by \(W=0\) and exhibits no conventional critical behavior. Our findings show that thermodynamic topology provides a global characterization of equilibrium configurations that complements conventional temperature-based criticality analysis, and that the global winding number alone does not uniquely determine the existence of conventional critical points.

papers.title: Flat Space Entanglement from Wedge Holography
papers.abstract: We study holographic entanglement entropy in three-dimensional flat space by combining wedge holography with a controlled flat limit of AdS end-of-the-world branes. The limit takes a wedge of AdS$_4$ bounded by two AdS$_3$ branes to a Randall-Sundrum-like configuration of two flat branes, and the entanglement entropy of an interval in the two-dimensional corner CFT becomes that of an interval at null infinity of the branes. The result has the functional form of the entanglement entropy of a two-dimensional Carrollian CFT, the proposed holographic dual of gravity in asymptotically flat three-dimensional spacetimes. However, the inferred central charges yield $c_M=0$ and $c_L\to\infty$ in the flat limit. Adding a gravitational Chern-Simons term produces a $c_M$-like contribution, but we still find $c_L\to\infty$ and $c_M\to0$ in this limit. Moreover, the corresponding extremal surfaces do not approach the swing surfaces proposed by Song and collaborators. Instead, they collapse onto null rays along null infinity. We argue that both features are generic for flat limits of AdS/CFT. They follow from entanglement entropy being a property of the domain of dependence and from the equality of causal and entanglement wedges for intervals in the vacuum.

papers.title: Exact Mass Multipoles of Distorted Schwarzschild Spacetimes
papers.abstract: Using the isolated-horizon framework, we compute the geometric and mass multipole moments of the Weyl-distorted Schwarzschild horizon without linearizing the distortion. Starting from the exact integral representation we evaluate it in closed form for two cases, a pure quadrupole distortion and a dipole-quadrupole-octupole distortion. For a pure quadrupole we obtain a closed form for all $\ell$ in terms of confluent hypergeometric functions, while for a dipole-quadrupole-octupole distortion we derive a closed-form series solution in the odd-parity coefficient $β$ whose coefficients are exact in the quadrupole coefficient $α_{2}$. We use these results to understand the errors incurred by leading-order approximations. Leading-order approximations in $α_{2}$ misestimate every dimensionless mass multipole by a relative error of roughly $α_{2}$, nearly independent of $\ell$, and for pure linearization most of the error lies in the linearized quadrupole moment rather than the discarded higher multipoles. A simple degree-counting rule determines which orders of distortion contribute to each multipole. As a consequence, the odd-parity component must be small compared with $α_{2}^2$ before it can be neglected. Finally, truncating the series in $β$ at its first $β$-dependent order reproduces the $\ell \leq 6$ multipoles to about $10^{-3}$ for $|β|,|α_{2}| \leq 1/8$.

papers.title: Massless neutrinos in a left-right symmetric universe
papers.abstract: This comment is a comment stimulated by the 1957 Goldhaber et al. experiment, that detected a massless left-handed electron neutrino with negative helicity. The standard description of this neutrino is by means of a Weyl spinor. It is shown below that this description is incomplete, and in fact one needs a massless Dirac spinor to comply with the requirements of quantum field theory. A Dirac spinor is composed of two Weyl spinors. This in turn raises the necessity to explain the fate of the right-handed electron neutrino, partner of the Goldhaber et al. experiment's one. A possible explanation for its invisibility is suggested here in terms of a left-right symmetric extension of the standard model.

papers.title: Geometrothermodynamics characterization of ABG-AdS black hole immersed by string clouds
papers.abstract: Regular black holes, whose singular cores are replaced by smooth geometries sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics, provide a natural setting to study how thermodynamic stability is encoded in spacetime geometry. Conventional stability criteria, however, depend on the choice of thermodynamic potential. Here we develop the quasi-homogeneous geometrothermodynamics of the regular Ayón-Beato--García anti-de Sitter (ABG-AdS) black hole surrounded by a cloud of strings, a Legendre-invariant framework in which no potential needs to be preferred. We show that the entropy, electric monopole charge and AdS radius act as extensive variables obeying a generalized quasi-homogeneity condition, and that the equilibrium manifold then carries three families of thermodynamic metrics. We establish an exact correspondence between response-function anomalies and curvature singularities: the first metric's curvature diverges on the zero-temperature extremal boundary, where the heat capacity vanishes, signaling Davies first-order transitions, whereas the second's diverges precisely where the heat capacity does, pinpointing Davies second-order transitions. The Gibbs free energy displays a swallow-tail structure that reveals a first-order small/large black hole transition, whose metastable region is bounded by these divergences of the heat capacity, together with a Hawking--Page-type transition to thermal AdS. The string-cloud density and the electric charge jointly control the horizon structure, the admissible thermal domain and the stability intervals.

papers.title: Rømer all ears: An auditory analog of Ole Rømer's demonstration of the finite speed of light using smartphones as an acoustic vernier
papers.abstract: We present an undergraduate experiment for teaching Ole Rømer's 1676 method for demonstrating the finite speed of light. Two smartphones emit periodic sound pulses whose synchronization is evaluated directly by the participants' hearing, acting as an "acoustic vernier" that achieves millisecond travel-time resolution without microphones or external sensors. Because the measurement relies strictly on propagation delays between stationary stations, it establishes a direct experimental analogy to Rømer's original argument and dispenses with auxiliary wave phenomena absent from the 1676 analysis, such as acoustic beats or the Doppler effect. The pedagogical strength of the experiment lies precisely in this direct appeal to the senses. Loss of synchronization becomes perceptible starting at a separation of approximately 5 m and grows progressively clearer across several tens of meters. Despite its simplicity, systematic blind measurements determine the speed of sound in air with single-run uncertainties of 2 to 5 m/s (around 1%) and agree within 1.1% with theoretical predictions across ambient temperatures from 9 to 25 $^\circ$C. Beyond numerical measurement, anchoring the method in explicit sensory perception helps to clarify the recurring conceptual entanglement between Rømer's geometric delay and the kinematic Doppler effect, while highlighting how this same travel-time principle underpins contemporary astrophysical techniques, such as pulsar timing and eclipse timing variations (ETV).

papers.title: Flavor Alignment and Operator Sensitivity in a Left--Right Universal-Seesaw Model
papers.abstract: We analyse the flavour structure and low-energy operator sensitivity of a parity-related doublet universal-seesaw model with an imposed lepton triality. Degenerate bare singlet masses permit a basis in which light-light tree neutral flavour transitions vanish; the physical heavy masses remain nondegenerate. We connect this alignment property to the axial and scalar differences measured by $B_{d,s}^0\toμ^+μ^-$ and reproduce the six-state charged-vector mixing amplitudes for five reference masses. The reference analysis identifies kaon CP violation as the more sensitive flavour probe. Historical kaon data disfavour the lower reference masses, while estimates suggest that dimuon and radiative $B$-decay effects are harder to resolve at present precision. These comparisons use the specified reference spectrum and historical inputs. We also compare charged and neutral resonance rates with published search benchmarks. The vacuum hierarchy entails a cancellation of about $5\times10^{-6}$ at $M_{W_R}=80\,\mathrm{TeV}$. The initially thermal Dirac-neutrino branch has a dataset-dependent extra-radiation tension, strengthened in an illustrative mass-dependent decoupling estimate. For dimuon decays we establish operator selection rules and sensitivity estimates. The numerical flavour results cover meson mixing and charged-vector dipoles. We give no dimuon branching-fraction prediction or global allowed region.

papers.title: On the effective atmospheric-scale $Δm^2$ in neutrino oscillation
papers.abstract: We discuss an effective two-frequency description of the three-generation neutrino oscillation with the key quantity $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} }$, which unifies the effects of atmospheric-scale $Δm^2_{31}$-$Δm^2_{32}$ driven oscillations. As a solution to the minimization problem in vacuum, Nunokawa {\it et al.} obtained $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} } = Δm^2_{31} - (2E / L) \arctan \left\{ r_{2} \sin 2Δ_{21} / ( r_{1} + r_{2} \cos 2Δ_{21} ) \right\}$, where $Δ_{21} \equiv Δm^2_{21} L / (4 E)$ and $r_{i}$ are the mixing-angle dependent constants. Despite the skepticism for the $L/E$ dependence in this formula, we show, in fact, that this is an exact expression, which renders the probability formula also exact. We offer an appealing-to-intuition physical explanation for the $L/E$ dependence that it originates from the nature-designed three generation neutrinos. The way it is buried into $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} }$ is through the solar-effect renormalization to this quantity. With the physical interpretation of $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} }$ at hand, we aim at resolving the existing controversies on $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} }$ in this paper.

papers.title: DEC Fill-ins, the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, and positive mass theorems with untrapped boundary
papers.abstract: Given a closed $(n-1)$-dimensional manifold equipped with prescribed spacetime Bartnik data, we ask when this can be realised as the boundary of a compact $n$-dimensional initial data set satisfying the dominant energy condition (DEC). This is a natural generalisation of the problem of non-negative scalar curvature fill-ins, where the boundary metric and mean curvature are prescribed. We give conditions on the Bartnik data that suffice to prove the existence of such DEC fill-ins with inner MOTS boundary, and give some applications of these fill-ins. Our first application of these is a lower bound on the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, which we slightly reformulate here to be a genuine spacetime definition. Our other applications include proving a positive mass theorem for spin initial data with boundary that need not be trapped, and a spacetime Penrose-like inequality that gives a positive lower bound on the mass of an initial data set with boundary in terms of its boundary Bartnik data assuming the spacetime Penrose inequality holds.

papers.title: Background characterization in the PIKACHU Phase 1 search for two-neutrino double-beta decay of $^{160}$Gd
papers.abstract:
We report a background characterization for the search for two-neutrino double-beta ($2
u2β$) decay of $^{160}$Gd using Ce:Gd$_3$Al$_2$Ga$_3$O$_{12}$ scintillators in the PIKACHU experiment Phase 1 at the Kamioka underground laboratory. In particular, surface contamination of the crystal was identified through the characteristic distortion of the $^{214}$Po $α$-ray spectrum, leading to an improved background model that reproduces the observed energy spectra. No significant excess attributable to $^{160}$Gd $2
u2β$ decay was observed, yielding a lower limit of $T^{2ν}_{1/2} \geq 2.32 	imes 10^{19}$ yr at 90\% C.L. The established background model and analysis framework provide a foundation for future PIKACHU phases aiming to discover $^{160}$Gd $2

papers.title: Charge-resolved four-lepton probes of an $eμ$-flavour-violating scalar at FCC-ee
papers.abstract: We study a real neutral scalar $X$ with a single flavour-off-diagonal coupling $h_{eμ}=h_{μe}\equiv h$. The coupling induces associated production, $e^+e^-\to e^\pmμ^\mp X$, and the decay $X\to e^\pmμ^\mp$. The resulting four-lepton final state separates into the charge-balanced channel $e^+e^-μ^+μ^-$ and the same-sign same-flavour channels $e^\pm e^\pmμ^\mpμ^\mp$. The charge-balanced channel receives a large prompt continuum background, while the same-sign category has a small estimated background under our benchmark assumptions. We analyse the two channels at FCC-ee for $\sqrt{s}=240~\mathrm{GeV}$ and $\mathcal{L}=10.8~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, including a detector simulation. The collider sensitivities are compared with the one-coupling constraints from the electron and muon magnetic moments, muonium--antimuonium conversion, and LEP dilepton data. At $m_X=146~\mathrm{GeV}$, motivated by the largest excess in the CMS $eμ$ resonance search, the expected 95\% CL reach of the charge-balanced channel, including a 1\% background uncertainty, is $|h|\simeq 1.0 \times 10^{-2}$, while the same-sign channel reaches $|h|\simeq 1.7 \times 10^{-3}$, compared with the cesium-based electron-$g-2$ bound $|h|<1.46\times10^{-2}$. Both channels thus probe couplings below the present bound. The two signal rates are equal before selection; the difference in reach follows from the different backgrounds.

papers.title: Holographic Spread Complexity of a Probe Particle with General Initial Data
papers.abstract: We investigate the holographic spread complexity of a massive particle probing global AdS$_3$ with general initial data. By constructing an adapted Hamiltonian, we map each bulk geodesic to a boundary Krylov dynamical pair, whose dynamics are governed solely by the conserved chiral charges. We find that, for generic initial data, the original identification $\dot{C}\sim p_ρ$ fails; instead, both the complexity and its growth rate depend nonlinearly on the bulk Noether charges. We systematically analyze this nonlinear encoding via several perturbative expansions. We further investigate two refined variants: the symmetry-resolved spread complexity, which restores the bulk radial $π$-periodicity, and the chiral spread complexity, which admits an exact closed form approaching the standard complexity at small angular momentum. Finally, by directly quantizing an effective AdS$_2$ theory, we obtain a new holographic interpretation of spread complexity in terms of the lapse function.

papers.title: Exotic Portals for Hadronic Processes: The Gluon-Gluon and Gluon-Quark Portals
papers.abstract: In this work we explore all possible light exotic (LEX) particles which are accessible through the gluon-gluon ($g$-$g$) and gluon-quark ($g$-$q$) phenomenological portals up to effective dimension six. We present effective models for these new states, which are directly accessible through gluon and quark fusion processes, and which are guaranteed decays involving Standard Model (SM) quarks and gluons. We note many accessible states in particularly unusual SU(3)$_\text{c}$ representations, which contain large Clebsch-Gordan coefficients. We also include some interesting dimension seven operators with highly unusual features. We also consider all potential spin values for our LEX states, looking at Lorentz representations and color selection rules. In this, we find that states in various unusual Lorentz representations are accessible. We also find that certain operator types have restrictions on allowed color representations based on spin.

papers.title: Exact stress-tensor fluctuations from conformal symmetry and black hole radiation
papers.abstract: Semiclassical gravity is sourced by the expectation value of the stress tensor, and it is reliable only if the fluctuations around this value are small. In two dimensions, conformal symmetry captures the essential physics of Hawking radiation in its s-wave sector and determines the mean value exactly, for any background and any quantum state. We show that it also determines the local fluctuations of the null components $T_{\pm\pm}$. The square of the stress tensor is defined by the operator product expansion, up to a multiple $α$ of $\partial_\pm^2T_{\pm\pm}$ that labels point-splitting prescriptions. Its transformation law under the conformal map to locally inertial coordinates gives the variance in closed form. The relative fluctuation scales as $1/c$, with $c$ the central charge. For the Schwarzschild black hole it is $22/5c$ for the Hawking flux at infinity, that of flat-space thermal radiation. At the horizon it is $-44α/3c$ for the outgoing flux and $(238+720α)/5c$ for the ingoing flux that drives the backreaction. Both reduce to $22/5c$ for $α=-3/10$, which corresponds to the Möbius-covariant prescription. For large $c$ these results support the semiclassical approximation.

papers.title: Studies of dual ions arriving time reconstruction in N$ν$DEx time projection chamber
papers.abstract: The N$ν$DEx experiment aims to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay of \(^{82}\)Se with a high-pressure \(^{82}\)SeF\(_6\) negative-ion time projection chamber. In the assumed two-carrier model, the arrival-time separation of SeF\(_5^-\) and SeF\(_6^-\) can estimate the longitudinal coordinate without an external trigger. We compare FFT deconvolution and direct waveform fitting on simulated Topmetal-S charge-sensitive-amplifier waveforms. With the fixed amplifier response, direct fitting and FFT accepted 873 and 855 of 873 geometry-selected single depositions, respectively. On the 855 common events, the arrival-time separation RMSEs were 0.180 and 0.222 ms. Numerical depth calibration gave mean \(z\) residuals of 0.036 and 0.075 cm and RMSEs of 0.192 and 0.208 cm on 848 common events. With sampled CSA shaping, FFT accepted the same 855 waveforms and direct fitting accepted 866 of 873. On the four-way common sample of 855 events, the direct-fit separation RMSE was 0.180~ms with fixed shaping and 0.217~ms with sampled shaping. An accepted near-readout direct fit outside the FFT sample had a 184~ms separation error, giving an RMSE of 6.25~ms over all accepted sampled-response direct fits. With the fixed response, the full-track fit retained 1,185 of 1,810 observed pads in 100 selected Geant4 events. The median event-level depth RMSE was 0.184 cm. Subtracting each event's mean Monte Carlo residual gave a median event-centred RMS of 0.102 cm as a diagnostic of relative track shape. The absolute depth remains sensitive to the common event time. Validation with detector data is needed to assess the effects of diffusion, electronics noise, and inter-pad response.

papers.title: Neural Network Potential Reconstruction from Phase Shifts in Resonant $n+{}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ Scattering
papers.abstract: We reconstruct a local, energy-independent effective potential for the narrow $D_{3/2}$ resonance of $n+{}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ from elastic phase shifts, using a Gaussian-enveloped neural parametrization coupled to a differentiable variable-phase calculation and checked by independent radial Schrödinger solvers. For the first resonance (below $2.5$ MeV LAB), the reconstruction gives a $90^\circ$ crossing at $1.001$ MeV LAB and a derivative width of $85$ keV LAB. The published Dubovichenko potential gives similar values with its original kinetic coefficient. Four reconstructions with adjustable range place the crossing within $5$ keV of one another while their central potentials span $47$ MeV. This spread illustrates the radial ambiguity of the inversion for the measured $D_{3/2}$ phases. The broad $P_{3/2}$ resonance of $n+α$ serves as a benchmark for the same method.

papers.title: Boosted energy-energy correlators in the small-acoplanarity limit
papers.abstract: We study the energy-energy correlator in the hadronic decay of a boosted boson. We focus on the small-acoplanarity region, where the two hadron momenta are nearly back-to-back in the plane transverse to the boson momentum. We derive a transverse-momentum-dependent factorization formula for electroweak and Higgs bosons in this region, expressed directly in boosted-frame variables in terms of hard, soft, and jet functions with a one-dimensional recoil measurement. We verify its singular real-emission terms at next-to-leading order and present resummed predictions up to N$^3$LL for asymmetric $e^+e^-$ colliders. For vector bosons, the azimuthal orientation of the hadron pair about the boost axis is sensitive to the transverse-spin correlation of the produced quarks through the Collins fragmentation function. We study this sensitivity for photon-tagged $Z$ bosons in $e^+e^-\to Zγ$ and compare our predictions with simulations using PYTHIA 8 supplemented by StringSpinner.

papers.title: Quarkonium Energy Correlators in Proton-Proton Collisions: Analytic Calculation and Angular-Momentum Hierarchy
papers.abstract: We present the first complete leading-order (LO) analytic calculation of the quarkonium energy correlator (QEC) in $pp$ collisions, for the color-singlet ${}^3S_1^{[1]}$ and the color-octet ${}^1S_0^{[8]}$, ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$, and ${}^3P_J^{[8]}$ channels of $J/ψ$ production. Instead of the high-$p_T$ fragmentation approximation, the calculation retains the full kinematics of the recoil parton, inverts the map from transverse momentum to the rest-frame angle in closed form, and is validated by \textsc{HELAC-onia} in shape and absolute normalization. We also give the analytic counterpart of the $p_T$-weighted variant of the correlator. The LO shape of each channel is organized by the total angular momentum $J$ of the $c\bar c$ pair, as a consequence of the tree-level selection rule that forbids two on-shell gluons from forming a $J=1$ state. This hierarchy is compressed in the central sPHENIX acceptance and exposed by the wider forward coverage at the LHC. In the distribution normalized to the total cross section, much though not all of the scale uncertainty cancels, leaving promising distinctions in the QEC shapes between different $J/ψ$ production channels. The discriminating power of the QEC can be further improved by next-to-leading-order calculations and by utilizing QECs in simultaneous fits with the $p_T$ spectrum and polarization measurements.

papers.title: Refined Rényi Entropy from Replica-Geometry Tensor Networks
papers.abstract: Holographic tensor networks are a central route to understanding the mechanism behind the holographic duality, but standard fixed-graph constructions with maximally entangled links face a structural obstacle. Their leading entanglement spectra are flat, so their Rényi entropies do not depend on the replica index. This is in sharp contrast with holographic conformal field theories, where a tensionful cosmic brane makes the refined Rényi entropy $n$-dependent. Capturing this replica dependence is therefore an important test of tensor-network descriptions of holographic entanglement. We construct an explicit family of replica-dependent geodesic graphs that reproduces this behavior while keeping the links maximally entangled. For each replica index $n$, geodesics are emitted from the replicated boundary with the same local, isotropic intersection measure. They perfectly tessellate the selected replica geometry, so the $n$-dependence of their intersection counts comes from the geometry. Tensor-network models on these graphs reproduce the cosmic-brane prescription for refined Rényi entropy by counting crossing threads. Their cross-copy endpoint density also agrees, in CFT$_2$, with a boundary reconstruction within the additive linear combination proposal, providing a check beyond the total entropy. In higher dimensions, we further obtain an analytic large-separation decay law for this density.

papers.title: Completing the real-space construction of the canonical harmonic coordinates of Kerr metric
papers.abstract: In this paper, we determine the exact canonical harmonic Kerr metric to all post-Minkowskian (PM) orders within the multipolar post-Minkowskian (MPM) formalism. The metric agrees with the previously constructed 4PM results. Using a formal series ring, we prove that no homogeneous components of Laplacian operator appear in this metric at PM order $n\ge2$. Together with the equality of the linear field with the canonical Kerr solution, this property allows an inductive construction of the canonical MPM metric where all gauge moments vanish. The coordinate transformation linking the canonical harmonic Kerr metric to the Boyer-Lindquist metric is generated by the real part of a complex harmonic radial function. A recent independent construction by Sadu and Vanhove using momentum-space recursion and a residual homogeneous freedom classification yields the same result, providing a cross validation of the closed-form canonical harmonic Kerr metric.

papers.title: The Zero Enrichment Rare Objects (ZERO) Survey I: Photometric Calibration of NB395 and Metallicity Estimation
papers.abstract: We present the first results of the Zero Enrichment Rare Objects (ZERO) survey, a narrow-band photometric survey targeting metallicity-sensitive narrow bands using the Hyper Suprime-Cam on the Subaru Telescope. This paper outlines the scientific goals, survey strategy, current observational status, photometric calibration, and metallicity estimation. The current ZERO footprint comprises 21 pointings, covering approximately 35 deg$^2$ along the celestial equator in the NB395 band, reaching NB395 $\sim$ 24.5 mag (10$σ$) in one hour, significantly deeper than typical comparable narrow-band Ca H\&K surveys. The NB395 photometry is calibrated using corrected Gaia BP/RP spectra and the recalibrated SDSS Stripe 82 catalog, achieving a typical zero-point precision of $\sim$0.3 per cent and flat-field precision better than 1 per cent on spatial scales larger than 8$^\prime$. Under typical conditions (three repeats; total exposure time $\sim$1 hour), the photometric precision reaches $\sim$1.1 per cent at NB395 $\approx$ 12, $\sim$1.5 per cent at 20, and $\sim$10 per cent at 24. We estimate [Ca/H] using a Physics-constrained Stellar Locus Fitting Method. The resulting [Ca/H] precision is better than 0.18 dex for sources brighter than NB395 $\sim$ 20, spanning a wide metallicity range from metal-rich to the very metal-poor regime ($-3 \le$ [Ca/H]$\le +0.5$). We further show that NB395 traces [Ca/H] more directly than [Fe/H]. The final catalog contains one million sources with NB395 photometry, including 379,216 repeatedly observed and 61,845 with [Ca/H] estimates. These results provide a solid foundation for future ZERO survey, including photometric calibration, stellar parameter determination, and investigations of Galactic structure and chemical evolution.

papers.title: Dijet photoproduction in ep and eA collision in POWHEG
papers.abstract: We present the implementation of dijet photoproduction in electron-proton and electron-nucleus collisions in the POWHEG BOX V2 Monte Carlo event generator. The process is computed at next-to-leading order in QCD including both direct and resolved photon contributions and is consistently matched to parton showers using the POWHEG method. The implementation is validated by using POWHEG BOX V2 internal consistency checks as well as by comparing fixed-order results with SHERPA. We compare our predictions to dijet photoproduction data from DESY HERA I and II, finding good agreement within theoretical uncertainties, and provide predictions for both electron-proton and electron-gold collisions at the upcoming BNL EIC, illustrating its potential to further constrain both photon and nuclear parton distribution functions.

papers.title: Eigenvalue-based computation of Richardson pairing spectra and finite-size thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We present a numerical workflow for the reduced BCS Richardson model, combining the eigenvalue-based Bethe equations, Baxter-polynomial reconstruction, and complex root finding. Newton-Raphson iteration solves the nonlinear equations for the eigenvalue-based variables; a linear system yields the polynomial coefficients, and Laguerre iteration with polynomial deflation extracts the rapidities. We apply the procedure to equally spaced, quadratic, and hydrogen-like non-degenerate single-particle spectra as the pairing strength varies. For finite systems, we calculate canonical observables from the complete seniority-zero spectrum and check benchmark spectra against exact diagonalization. In an eight-level, four-pair system with a hydrogen-like spectrum, the heat capacity has two maxima at weak coupling. With increasing coupling, the low-temperature maximum shifts upward and the high-temperature maximum downward; the latter ceases to be a distinct local maximum near $g\simeq0.03515$ in the units used. The equally spaced benchmark instead has a single dominant maximum over the coupling interval displayed for that spectrum. This comparison illustrates how single-particle level spacings can shape finite-size thermal response. The C++ code is publicly available; numerical instabilities remain possible near ill-conditioned configurations and at larger sizes.

papers.title: AI-assisted formal proofs for static and time-dependent density functional theory on lattices
papers.abstract: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem fails on lattices, where two potentials that differ by more than a constant can share a ground state. We prove that such potentials are exceptional. We consider spinless fermions on any connected lattice, at any filling other than empty or full, with hopping amplitudes of a common sign and any density-density interaction. The potentials whose ground state is shared with a potential differing by more than a constant lie in a closed, nowhere dense set of zero Lebesgue measure. The densities of non-degenerate shared ground states form a set of codimension at least two. The statement about the potentials also holds for the Kohn-Sham potential and for spin-density functional theory, where a uniform shift of the magnetic field is the only additional freedom. In time-dependent density functional theory on lattices, we show that not every ground state of a connected lattice can serve as the initial state of the density-potential map. A counterexample is the ground state of two fermions on a square that Penz and van Leeuwen found as a counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem. For almost every static potential, however, every real ground state can serve as an initial state, also for spin-resolved densities. We also give formal proofs that the time-dependent Kohn-Sham potential exists, locally in time, for almost every static Kohn-Sham potential, and of known results: local existence and uniqueness of the time-dependent potential for an admissible initial state, continuation in time up to the boundary of the set of admissible states, and the convergence properties of a regularized Kohn-Sham iteration. All theorems and propositions are formalized in the proof assistant Lean 4 and checked by computer.

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Moduli Stabilization with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ Modular Symmetry
papers.abstract: We study the stabilization of the three complex moduli associated with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ modular symmetry by gaugino condensation in $\mathcal N=1$ supergravity models from heterotic string theory, where one-loop threshold corrections fix both the modular weight and the singularity structure of the superpotential. We determine, for each threshold class, the complete parametrization of the consistent superpotential relying on Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ basic modular-invariant ratios and their syzygies, generalizing the insufficient SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$-inspired techniques based solely on polynomials of its absolute invariants. This structure supports a rich landscape of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua. Unlike in the SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$ case, higher-order zeros produce continuous surfaces and curves of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua, while, among the six isolated fixed points, only those with $S_4$ and $D_{12}$ residual symmetries can stabilize all three moduli. We also construct isolated vacua away from fixed points, some of which lie at the moduli values preferred by genus-two modular flavor fits, and examine the suppression of the geometric moduli masses near an enhanced-symmetry point.

papers.abstract: Gluon tomography of the nucleon through hard-exclusive electroproduction of $J/ψ$ has been one of the key motivations for Electron-Ion Collider. However, the next-to-leading order (NLO) perturbative QCD calculations available in the literature were performed either in the collinear factorization limit where the heavy-quark mass is neglected, or in heavy-quark limit where the heavy quarkonia are approximately point-like. We present a full next-to-leading order collinear factorization for the hard exclusive production of heavy mesons that retains the meson mass as well as full light-cone distribution amplitude. We compare the full NLO result with the special limits and estimate the errors due to potentially-large corrections from $α_s(M)$ and $M^2/Q^2$ at this order.

papers.title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
papers.abstract: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) encode the non-perturbative structure of hadrons in terms of their partonic constituents. They are defined through matrix elements containing parton operators that are connected by a Wilson line along a light-front direction, which makes them difficult to access in Euclidean lattice calculations. We demonstrate how parton functions can be directly obtained in Minkowski space using the Hamiltonian framework. We compute fermion and antifermion PDFs, LCDAs, and decay constants of the vector meson in the Schwinger model for several fermion masses. States in Hilbert space are efficiently represented by tensor networks, with an expressivity that is systematically controlled by a bond dimension. The light-front Wilson line is implemented as a stepwise evolution on the lattice that alternates spatial shifts of an external charge with Trotterized time-evolution steps acting on a matrix product state. All systematic uncertainties are quantified by varying and extrapolating in the lattice spacing, volume, bond dimension, gauge-field truncation, and Trotter step width. The slow growth of the entanglement entropy makes moderate bond dimensions sufficient, which supports the feasibility of using tensor networks for computing light-front matrix elements in more general settings. We confirm that the computed distributions fulfill the expected normalizations, momentum sum rules, and symmetry properties.
